finding: prepare_data_from_y overwrites the first selected forecast column with ones in both train and adaptive blocks.
consequence: One actual ensemble member is silently discarded while the reported member count is unchanged.
remediation: The publication loader removes only explicit CSV index columns and retains every forecast column.

finding: The legacy history has m*tau+tau columns and fills the final tau columns with ones; the manuscript defines exactly m*tau lagged member errors.
consequence: The implemented decision rule has undocumented features and a different parameter dimension.
remediation: build_error_histories constructs exactly m*tau causal error features and exports history counts.

finding: The normalized-history expression is evaluated but not assigned.
consequence: The err_rule_norm option has no effect.
remediation: Normalization is implemented in-place and tested.

finding: The principal historical fit minimizes squared loss plus separate squared penalties on beta_t, beta0, and V0.
consequence: This is neither the paper's nonsquared norm-plus-norm robust counterpart nor the two-hyperparameter method described in the manuscript.
remediation: The new code labels and separates quadratic_stacked and exact norm_plus_norm objectives; both are reported.

finding: The historical search is 5x5x5x4=500 combinations of three penalties and a window.
consequence: The paper understates both model-selection degrees of freedom and total search cost.
remediation: Every new method uses an explicit, exported chronological validation grid; full-search runtime is benchmarked.

finding: The method called Exp3 observes every member loss and produces a deterministic weighted forecast.
consequence: It is a full-information Hedge-style forecaster, not a bandit-feedback Exp3 experiment.
remediation: The baseline is named Hedge and a separate Fixed Share tracker is included.

finding: The historical expert weights are initialized using the number of observations rather than the number of members.
consequence: Weights need not sum to one and the baseline can be numerically distorted.
remediation: All expert trackers initialize to 1/m and use stable log/softmax updates.

finding: Best Model in Hindsight is selected on the test segment and presented beside deployable methods.
consequence: It is an oracle diagnostic rather than a usable forecasting policy.
remediation: The new outputs label oracle_best_member as diagnostic_only and add validation_best_member as a deployable comparator.

finding: MAPE divides directly by y on a synthetic target that crosses zero.
consequence: Synthetic MAPE is undefined or dominated by values arbitrarily close to zero.
remediation: Primary synthetic metrics are MAE, RMSE, exact CVaR, sMAPE, and WAPE; safe MAPE reports its valid fraction.

finding: Empirical CVaR is formulated as a Gurobi model although the finite-sample value is an exact upper-tail average.
consequence: This adds avoidable solver cost and leaves the fractional boundary convention implicit.
remediation: empirical_cvar implements the exact finite-sample tail mass, including fractional boundary weight.

finding: energy_y_test_val.csv is headerless but is read with header inference.
consequence: The first target can be interpreted as a column name and lost, shifting forecast/target alignment.
remediation: load_energy reads the target with header=false and verifies exact 4929/1973/2956 split counts.

finding: The stored energy forecast columns do not exactly match the ten member identities listed in the manuscript.
consequence: The source of the reported energy table is ambiguous.
remediation: Both stored member labels and manuscript labels are exported in the dataset manifest with an explicit warning.

finding: The historical Passive-Aggressive update has fragile dimensions and insufficient zero-denominator protection.
consequence: Very poor PA results can be an implementation or tuning artifact.
remediation: The new PA-I predicts before updates, guards norms, and tunes C and epsilon on the same validation segment.

finding: The historical RLS covariance update lacks symmetry and numerical safeguards and has no common tuning protocol.
consequence: Instability or unfair defaults can affect the dynamic-baseline comparison.
remediation: The new RLS symmetrizes P, protects denominators, and tunes forgetting and ridge values chronologically.

finding: Historical synthetic defaults differ from the manuscript's 4000-point design and some driver failures are caught without failing the run.
consequence: A run can finish without producing the intended experiment or the paper's data-generating process.
remediation: The new generator is manuscript-faithful by default; task failures are collected and make the stage fail.

finding: The North Atlantic and Eastern Pacific ATCF/Hurricast matrices referenced by the Julia scripts are absent.
consequence: The hurricane table cannot be independently regenerated from the supplied archive.
remediation: The new loader fails explicitly and documents the required filenames/schema rather than substituting data.

finding: The handling of insufficient error history and new-storm boundaries is not fully specified in the legacy code.
consequence: Cold-start behavior can leak prior-event outcomes or vary across implementations.
remediation: The new causal history zero-pads unavailable slots (beta0 fallback), enforces verification delay, and supports reset/carry stress tests.
